# External benchmark corpus — provenance

## Source

- **Dataset:** [`BothBosu/multi-agent-scam-conversation`](https://huggingface.co/datasets/BothBosu/multi-agent-scam-conversation)
- **Upstream commit:** `709db2b6c37f424c3070f29138abb33971e21ab9`
- **Upstream files:** `agent_conversation_train.csv`, `agent_conversation_test.csv`
- **Retrieved:** 2026-09-07
- **Upstream CSV sha256:**
  - train — `e1c89f4e252162f5a37c01d2ebe9e0cdcad3b22b7bcf01ef730877cef04612db`
  - test  — `93d380c704e47d81028aa55c03a3f28cd6e23498c03cb70aad136a3762c0cc74`

## What it is

1 600 English phone-call dialogues (1 280 train + 320 test), balanced
800 scam / 800 non-scam. The dialogues are **synthetic** — generated by
Llama-3-70B — not transcripts of real calls. Eight scenario `type`s, four
per label:

| label  | `type`s |
|--------|---------|
| fraud  | `refund`, `reward`, `ssn`, `support` |
| benign | `appointment`, `delivery`, `insurance`, `wrong` (wrong number) |

None are bank-impersonation — this set exercises RingFence's cross-domain
coverage (refund, prize/sweepstakes, government/SSN, tech-support) against
scam scripts it was **not** tuned on.

## Vendored form

`multi_agent_scam_conversation.jsonl.gz` — one JSON object per line,
regenerable with `python corpus/external/build_snapshot.py` (needs network):

```json
{"id": "mas_train_0000", "split": "train", "label": "benign",
 "source_type": "appointment",
 "turns": [{"role": "CALLEE", "text": "Hello."},
           {"role": "CALLER", "text": "Hi, this is Karen ..."}, ...]}
```

- **sha256:** `20f046a20608044ef5c399b553b6e56270fa75dd969547ca2eafd53bfd3e7f05`
  (gzip written with `mtime=0`, so this is stable across rebuilds).
- The upstream `dialogue` string runs turns together with `Innocent:` /
  `Suspect:` prefixes. We split on those, map **`Suspect` → `CALLER`**
  (the party who phoned in — the potential scammer) and **`Innocent` →
  `CALLEE`** (the protected party), and strip the prefixes. The upstream
  `personality` column is dropped.
- **No timestamps** are stored — `packages/eval/external.py` synthesises a
  timeline at load time (see `docs/EXTERNAL_BENCHMARK.md`).

The upstream dataset card declares no licence. Included here solely as a

drop `multi_agent_scam_conversation.jsonl.gz` and keep `build_snapshot.py`
